node.title: Prepare work order
node.instructions: Read the project bridge, open the work order through xc-open-work-order, validate requested feature IDs without creating features, determine and validate work_order.document_language through xc-document from the explicit parameter or initiating user request, and record the requested scope. Write the report commitment work_order.requires_report in this same preparation step, resolved through the report policy rather than from the mode alone: an explicit user instruction first, then the project bridge which may only tighten, then report.default in the workshop configuration, then the built-in default. The shipped code-change-only tier means true for create, change, repair, and maintenance and false for investigation and review, and true when the mode cannot be confirmed, because an unknown mode is never interpreted as no report needed. Record work_order.report_skip_reason whenever the report is deliberately skipped, and capture work_order.report_baseline once, as the baseline commit, the worktree digest and the digest algorithm, and only when that resolved commitment is true: a work order that resolves to no report captures nothing, and the record keeps its three values and its publishable --format keys form. Where version control is unusable for the repository - it is not a worktree, or no baseline commit is resolvable - the capture fails closed and copies nothing; a full copy is admissible only through the explicit consent opt-in of the capture command, whose reference must name the user's explicit decision obtained through a main-session gate, and no new configuration item exists for it. The commitment, the initial report strength and, when the commitment is true, the baseline record are preparation-phase records, never retrospective notes, and a missing commitment fails this node.
node.deliverables: An authoritative workbench and explicit feature associations.
node.acceptance: The workbench is independent, feature associations are explicit, work_order.document_language is set before any document write, no unmanaged feature directory was created, and the mode-derived report commitment is written rather than assumed: work_order.requires_report carries the value the resolved report policy produced, every skip records one of the legal work_order.report_skip_reason values (read_only_mode, zero_analyzable_units, user_waived, policy_default), work_order.report_baseline records the baseline commit, the worktree digest and the digest algorithm only when the resolved commitment is true, a capture where version control was unusable failed closed with nothing copied unless the explicit consent opt-in of the capture command carried a reference naming the user's explicit decision, and a missing commitment fails this node.

result.summary: Workbench 20261030-1819-mc-2d-sandbox opened under an independent workshop worktree; feature_ids=[] validated (no feature created); work_order.document_language=en validated from the explicit parameter; report commitment written as requires_report=false with report_skip_reason=user_waived by explicit user instruction, so no baseline or report group; L1 convention discovery ran (not-applicable, record artifact); requested scope recorded from the prompt: standard create lifecycle, playable offline 2D sandbox, quality contract, visual review, no commit.
result.validation: prepare-work-order acceptance: independent workbench (separate workshop Git worktree), explicit empty feature associations, document language set before any document write, no feature directory created, report commitment + legal skip reason written, report baseline correctly absent because the commitment is false, convention discovery status and record published.

node.title: Repair spatial aid with a minimap
node.instructions: Remediate medium finding D3. Add a compact live minimap: a canvas element in index.html near the HUD, styled in css/style.css as a small glass panel that survives 960/800/1280 layouts; add renderMinimap(minimapCtx, world, player, camera) in render.js drawing the surface profile, underground tint, player dot and current viewport rectangle; in main.js size it for DPR, render it each frame (throttling is fine) and show a seed label. Add Node tests for the renderer (columns drawn, player dot, viewport rect, world bounds) and extend tools/journey_check.js to assert the minimap exists, is non-blank and changes after a teleport. Update README architecture and controls. Keep the accepted palette and all prior behavior. Run node --test, page_check and the journey probe; record evidence.
node.deliverables: Live minimap with surface profile, player dot and viewport, styled and tested; repair artifact.
node.acceptance: Minimap exists, renders non-blank under all layouts, tracks the player and viewport, and passes tests and the journey probe.

result.summary: Repair D3: added a live minimap panel (seed, surface profile, viewport rectangle, amber player dot) rendered by renderMinimap and wired through main with DPR sizing, seed updates and resize handling. Orientation checks pass in the browser (non-blank, tracks teleport). Tests 121/121, page check green, journey 70/70.
result.validation: Renderer tests assert columns/player dot/viewport; live browser checks assert existence, non-blank rendering and a changed image after moving the player. Final and 1280 screenshots inspected.

node.title: Recheck review findings and final score
node.instructions: Post-remediation recheck of the independent M2D-SES v1.1 review. Read visual-review.md, the three repair artifacts and the current journey report. Re-run the M2D-SES journeys against the fixed page (use tools/journey_check.js and inspect the fresh screenshots: mining-progress.png, underground.png, underground-floor.png, final-960x600.png, wide-1280x800.png, day/night/paused). Verify each required finding's closure condition: D1 sealed floor refuses a real mouse mine attempt with an unchanged block and dark underground background; D2 a live break-progress state with visible cracks and pickaxe swing completes into removal; D3 a live minimap exists, is non-blank, tracks the player and survives 960/800/1280. Re-score the ten PES domains and five ECS domains with the M2D-SES v1.1 anchors, apply defect caps and the G1-G3 gate, and record the final PES, ECS, composite and remaining observations. Write visual-recheck.md with the closure table, the final score and any residual limitation. Do not modify product code.
node.deliverables: visual-recheck.md with finding closure, re-run evidence, final M2D-SES v1.1 scores and gate.
node.acceptance: Every required finding is closed or explicitly carried with evidence; final PES/ECS/composite and gate recorded; dimensions use the M2D-SES v1.1 anchors.

result.summary: Recheck: all three required findings closed (sealed floor with real-click refusal and dark underground, live break progress with crack/pickaxe and browser evidence, live minimap tracking the player). Re-run: tests 121/121, page check green, journey 70/70 with 0 exceptions/console errors. Final M2D-SES v1.1: PES 69.2 / ECS 80.0 / composite 71.9, gate pass, 0 high/medium defects, 1 low observation (no save indicator).
result.validation: Every closure condition re-executed against the fixed page with screenshots and hashes; scores use the v1.1 anchors and caps; residual limitations recorded.

node.title: Produce change review report
node.instructions: Produce the change report for this work order after verification and before the result document. The group is mounted by the commitment value work_order.requires_report. Embed the xc-change-report subtree once under this group, or run a single role=report node that carries the same contract. Resolve the subtree's template path from the committed setup record at .agents/.xcoding-setup/manifest.json, which holds the installed xc-change-report package's absolute path; change-report-template.xml is read from it, and the host-to-Skill-root table is the fallback for a project with no such record. Before the group's first node runs, publish all thirteen caller-seeded keys with the values this work order actually uses, never merely accepting their declared defaults: report.path, report.manifest_path, report.baseline_commit, report.baseline_digest, report.language, report.strength, report.gate_required, report.gate_outcome, report.gate_rework_required, report.gate_recovery_required, report.round, report.refresh_count, and report.refresh_reason. report.round is the 1-based index of the pass being entered. When prepare-manifest measures one or more analyzable units, produce the report; when it measures zero analyzable units, record work_order.report_skip_reason=zero_analyzable_units and produce no report; a user waiver records work_order.report_skip_reason=user_waived, and a skip the resolved report policy produced records work_order.report_skip_reason=policy_default. A skipped gate records report.gate_outcome=not-run, never accepted.
node.deliverables: On the produced outcome: one change-report.html, one change-report-manifest.json, and one change-report-verdicts.json under the workbench report node artifact directory. On the skipped outcome: no report file is required, and the deliverable is the recorded work_order.report_skip_reason with report.run_required=false.
node.acceptance: Exactly one of the two outcomes holds: either the report exists at report.path and is proven by report.manifest_path, or report.run_required is false and work_order.report_skip_reason records one of the legal reasons (read_only_mode, zero_analyzable_units, user_waived, policy_default); a produced report is never accepted without its manifest, and a skip is never accepted without its reason. The caller publishes all thirteen caller-seeded report.* keys with the values this work order uses before the group's first node runs, and the subtree's template is resolved from the installed package path the setup record holds, so the guards and completion-fact selectors the subtree evaluates resolve against those thirteen declarations or against a key one of the subtree's own nodes writes before that expression reads it.

node.title: Write or revise document
node.instructions: Read document.path, document.template, document.inputs, document.contract, document.content_language, and document.authoring_requirements from the supplied blackboard and node references. Follow the public xc-document human-readable authoring default unless explicit document.authoring_requirements override its style preferences. Preserve exact commands, identifiers, paths, logs, and machine output where literal accuracy matters. Write or revise the target document immediately, preserve valid frontmatter, and do not read the runtime XML directly.
node.deliverables: The managed document at document.path.
node.acceptance: The target document exists, follows its domain and human-readable authoring contracts plus explicit user requirements, preserves key information, and has complete YAML frontmatter.

result.summary: Wrote result.md: actual changes inventory, validation evidence (121/121 tests, page check, 70/70 journey checks), capability and journey coverage, independent review as-found and post-repair M2D-SES v1.1 scores, baseline synchronization (none), deviations and residual risks (no user gates, report waived, no commit, isolation, same-agent review, coverage/audio/save-indicator/minimap limitations, review-artifact process deviation), the fixed report line, and the work order record.
result.validation: Result document records every lifecycle stage, the exact commands and outcomes, the review findings and closure, the final score and all residual risks; report obligation is an explicit user-waived skip.

node.title: Validate draft document
node.instructions: Run xc-document validation for document.path and document.kind.
node.deliverables: A validation result recorded in the node result.
node.acceptance: xc-document validates the draft without errors.

result.summary: xc-document validated result.md draft.
result.validation: Exit 0, ok=true, receipt passed.

node.title: Review document
node.instructions: Review document.path against the domain review dimensions, explicit document.authoring_requirements, and the public xc-document human-readable dimensions: audience fit, progressive disclosure, first-use terminology explanations, concision, and preservation of key information. Write findings to the declared node artifact and set document.review.open_issues to true or false through the runtime.
node.deliverables: A review artifact with prioritized findings and closure criteria.
node.acceptance: The review distinguishes required findings from optional observations, covers domain correctness and human readability, and sets document.review.open_issues.

node.title: Revise document from review
node.instructions: Read the latest review artifact and document.authoring_requirements, then revise only document.path. Apply the public xc-document human-readable authoring default except where explicit requirements override style preferences. Preserve document.content_language, valid frontmatter, exact technical evidence, and key information, then record the updated document as the node artifact.
node.deliverables: An updated managed document.
node.acceptance: Required domain and human-readability findings are resolved or explicitly escalated to a user gate.

node.title: Confirm document decisions
node.instructions: Present the document-specific decisions to the user. Record short choices in the blackboard and create revision nodes when feedback changes the document.
node.deliverables: Structured user decisions or an explicit continuation decision.
node.acceptance: Required user decisions are recorded and any necessary revision nodes are scheduled.

node.title: Validate final document
node.instructions: Run xc-document validation for document.path and document.kind after review and user decisions.
node.deliverables: A final validation result recorded in the node result.
node.acceptance: xc-document validates the final document without errors.

result.summary: Final xc-document validation of result.md passed.
result.validation: Exit 0, ok=true, receipt validated.

node.title: Finalize ordinary work order
node.instructions: Confirm the work order result, declared artifacts, feature baseline synchronization, code provenance, and residual risks, then close the work order. Consume work_order.report_skip_reason: when work_order.requires_report is true and neither a report path nor one of the legal skip reasons (read_only_mode, zero_analyzable_units, user_waived, policy_default) is recorded, the work order must not close.
node.deliverables: A completed, failed, or blocked work order with durable evidence.
node.acceptance: The runtime tree and workbench documents accurately describe the work order outcome, and a committed report obligation is either satisfied by a report path or explicitly recorded as a skip decision.

result.summary: Work order complete: goal, analysis, solution, self-approved solution gate, two implementation units, three verification units, an independent M2D-SES v1.1 visual review with three required findings, three remediation units and a recheck are recorded and validated. Final score PES 69.2 / ECS 80.0 / composite 71.9, gate pass, 0 high/medium defects. The report is an explicit user-waived skip (requires_report=false, report_skip_reason=user_waived); no project commit was created; no feature baseline exists.
result.validation: All top-level documents validated by xc-document (goal, analysis, solution, result); every node artifact exists and was validated; runtime integrity valid; objective and result sources are terminal document writers; convention discovery recorded as not-applicable; report obligation legally skipped; the verification, review and recheck evidence prove the requested capabilities and the fixed defects.
